source_material.title: KESPA Conversation Engine + SQL-Driven Personality Contract

source_material.description: Current generated KESPA public research manifest through KESPA-NOTE-026, used for deduplication and sequential ID allocation.

directly_recorded_facts: KESPA implemented a Conversation Engine plus SQL-driven Personality Contract baseline.
The stated goal is to keep normal personality tuning out of phrase-specific Brain patches.
The Conversation Engine evaluates the current turn using current message/context, recent tone, durable communication preferences, and global SQL-backed rules.
The engine records named personality dimensions and selects among named conversational postures.
Current serious situational context has higher precedence than ordinary persistent communication preferences.
The engine can use durable communication-preference memories while avoiding persistent transient emotional-state profiling.
brain_config is the runtime behavior/configuration control plane for the Conversation Engine.
A machine-readable personality contract is compiled for the current response.
Brain receives the contract, generates a response, validates style compliance, and can perform style-only repair.
The current Brain build is dev-019-personality-contract-v2.
The current local model is qwen2.5-coder:7b-instruct-q4_K_M.
Live tests in the supplied update show casual, celebratory, and supportive response behavior.
At least one supportive response still requires wording polish.
Normal personality tuning is intended to occur through SQL/Admin configuration rather than repeated Brain changes.
A deterministic conversation regression suite and personality-quality metrics are future work.
